Griffin Survivor Extreme-Duty Military Case for the iPad 4/3/2, Pink/Black (GB35379) With 3 little tech savvy kids in the house, ages 2-6, the electronics are a big draw. They hold a lot of appeal for the kids, but it's almost a constant stream of "oops!" as things are dropped when the kids move around or in a scuffle behind mom and dad's back. Not to mention how uncoordinated and clumsy I am by myself. If the iPad were less expensive like my Kindle Fire, I would probably go for a case that is more style than function, and a basic screen protector sheet. As it is, I have no desire to either replace the glass, or worse, buy a new iPad, so I got the super functional, heavy duty case. It's easy for the kids to pull them out, and putting them back requires taking the iPad out of the case, replacing the hinged covers, then going through the effort of putting the iPad back. After doing that once, I just leave them off now. I wish there was no way for them to come off, but it isn't a deal breaker for me.

text_fidelity_a:
Bluetooth Headphones, Soundcore Spirit Sports Earbuds by Anker, Bluetooth 5.0, 8H Battery, IPX7 Waterproof, SweatGuard, Comfortable Wireless Headphones, Secure Fit for Running, Gym, Workout These are around the same price as all the junky Chinese wireless earbud brands on Amazon but sound much better, are much more reliable, and are made by a company with good customer service that stands behind their products.

Ankers has several wireless earbuds with the cords that go behind the neck but only these, the spirit, the spirit pro, and the spirit x are worth considering for purchase. Their other earbuds are older models that cost just as much but have less features and weaker specs.

The bass on these is weak but I use these mostly for working out and for that it is fine.

I already have a pair of Apple EarPods but I wanted another wireless pair of headphones as well so I could switch back and forth while the other pair was charging.

These do not work with Apples w1 chip Bluetooth protocol, only apple and beats headphones work with that standard right now so those wireless headphones brands will sound better than anything other wireless headphones will with Apple products.

They also do not have aptx, which is the best sounding Bluetooth standard for anything other than Apple.

Ankers spirit pro headphones do support the aptx standard and supposedly have better bass than these so those are that models advantages.

However the spirit pro cost twice as much as these and only supports Bluetooth protocol 4.1 while these headphones support Bluetooth protocol 5.0.

Why is that important? Because the 5.0 protocol is the new “low energy” Bluetooth standard. Meaning that if you have both a device and headphones that support it you will get much more play time out of the same size battery.

Ankers other most recent model of earbuds, the spirit x headphones, have the same specs as these headphones in terms of the protocols they support but have a different form factor, obviously, and have 10mm drivers while these have 6mm. They also have a little more battery life.

I think I might buy the spirit x headphones as well in order to have a backup and to compare their sound.

As an Apple user the spirit pro headphones are just not worth the extra cost for me since I will never use the aptx protocol and they do not even support the Bluetooth 5.0 protocol.
If they were Bluetooth 5.0 compatible I might consider spending the extra 25 bucks in order to get that extra bass.

While these don’t sound spectacular they will get great battery life when I use them with devices that support 5.0 Bluetooth and they are very affordable.

I want to quickly rant about amazons policies and the flood of cheap Chinese products on here.

If you search for “wireless earbuds” or “Bluetooth earbuds” or any similar terms ankers products will not even show up on the first several pages of results.
Nor will Aukeys headphones, which I think are the second best option for wireless headphones in this price range.

Why is this?
Because the Chinese brands pay “click farms” to leave hundreds or even thousands of 5 star reviews.

The fraud is so obvious. What do you think is happening when a product has more than a thousand 5 star reviews all left on the same day or within the same few days and almost none of those reviews are from verified buyers?
The fact that many of them say the same things over and over and that many of them are written in broken English are other obvious clues.

I reported a few of them but Amazon does not take them down because Amazon cares about money and absolutely nothing else and having millions of people purchase this Chinese junk off their website makes them a lot of money.

It really sucks because good products, like these anker headphones, are barely visible in amazon search results because reputable brands don’t pay click farms to manipulate amazon search results.

It’s the consumers that lose in the end when their headphones, or other cheap Chinese products, break a few weeks after use or maybe never even work to begin with.
And you can bet that half of the time the companies selling this junk on amazon will simply disappear in order to avoid accepting returns and then reappear later under a new seller account to sell more junk through click farm manipulated amazon search results.

Of course amazon will find itself on the hook for some of these costs but apparently the money they make off of allowing all of this Chinese junk to be sold on their website under false practices is much more than any costs they incur.

These practices that amazon allows, and this one issue about manipulated search results is just the tip of the iceberg, hurts not just American consumers it also hurts American companies.

Rant over.
text_fidelity_b: Bluetooth Headphones, Soundcore Spirit Sports Earbuds by Anker, Bluetooth 5.0, 8H Battery, IPX7 Waterproof, SweatGuard, Comfortable Wireless Headphones, Secure Fit for Running, Gym, Workout

text_fidelity_a:
Epson VS230 SVGA 3LCD Projector, 2800 Lumens Color Brightness I also have an Epson EX7220 WXGA projector with 3000/3000 color/white lumens. Both are excellent projectors that have surprised me by their ease of use and great clarity even in lit rooms. But the EX7220 costs about 50% more, while the two projectors come in the exact same form factor (i.e., the casing, buttons, and remote are 99.5% identical). Additionally, there are loads of other Epson projectors in their lineup, all priced differently, so what do you get when you spend more money?

1) Resolution. I just now realized how important this is. Although I was surprised just how well both projectors play movies from my computer projected onto a wall (even a light yellow or a light brown wall, without the color of the picture seeming to suffer), I now realize that you should pick a resolution that matches your computer's resolution or your computer's ability to send out the projector's native resolution.

For example, my computer's native resolution is WXGA and so is the EX7220's, so I can mirror my monitor's image on the wall (which is what you'll probably do in most situations - especially presentations - so you can see what is happening on your small screen. The alternative is to "extend" your desktop onto the wall, which in some cases can output a different resolution, but this is not as practical in most cases, particularly presentations) with a perfect match from computer to projector. However, when I connect the VS330 in XGA resolution (with a 4:3 ratio), it looks good, but there is black, unused space all around the actual image because the resolutions are in different formats. The black area is basically wasted pixels. You can put it in 4:3 mode, but you're getting a degraded (although still sharp) image on the wall.

Just as monitors have gotten higher in resolution over time, projectors are not far behind. But you definitely pay for the difference. For basic work presentations and casual video watching, 1024x768 is fine. As you want to put more information on one screen or watch high definition movies in your free time, you'll want to look at a higher end monitor.

2. Luminescence. There is now an official standard to differentiate between color lumens and white lumens, whereas in the past only lumens were specified. I am fully convinced that color lumens matter, particularly for presentations where visual content matters and especially for video watching. That said, I am amazed how great movies look projected onto a large, empty wall, and it surprises me that more people don't watch everything via projector. I'd never buy a projector that didn't specify color lumens. And, clearly, you pay exponentially for a greater color lumen output.

3. Accessories. The VS330 lacks the carry bag, wireless connection dongle (although it comes with the bracket that now I have to be sure not to lose in case I'd ever get the dongle), and extra cables that come with the EX7220. Not a big deal by any standards, although I do like the (very basic) carry bag that comes with the EX7220.

To speak specifically to this projector, I am really impressed how easy it is to set up and get working correctly. It's basically plug and play, eliminating most of the risk of those embarrassing moments where no one can get the projector to work. Most of the functionality also comes through the remote as well. You can also put the sound through the projector, and I love the retractable tilting foot on the device. It's small, boots up quickly, is easy to use, and is really impressive with its picture, even for playing movies. That's a great side benefit, but as you start looking into its use as a movie machine, that's where you really start looking at higher end models, and it's hard to know where to stop, because they make a few models much more geared toward movies well beyond the EX7220.

This is a great machine. I'd recommend Epson to anyone based on my experience. As for which model to buy, I'd tell you to take a careful look at your needs. This model is great for ease of use and quality of picture for basic office uses.
text_fidelity_b: Epson VS230 SVGA 3LCD Projector, 2800 Lumens Color Brightness

Internet TV--horrible interface

To be honest, I wouldn't use most of these, so I'm not all that impressed with the Apps, though certainly they have the most needed on one in Netflix. text_fidelity_a:
ARCTIC Breeze Pro USB Desktop Fan with 4-Port USB Hub This review covers two different models of the Arctic fan:

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>Model with USB hub:
I have been using the original ARCTIC Breeze for a while and have been very pleased with its performance, and especially pleased with how quiet it runs. The Pro model builds on that and adds a few more useful features.

Unlike the original model which had a bendable stem with a USB plug on the end, the Pro has a base so the fan can be positioned away from the USB port on the PC. The attached power cord is a little over 5 feet long, making it possible to put the fan on my desk and plug it into the PC on the floor.

The base also has 4 USB input ports, so it works as a USB hub. It has a 5V power input jack if you want to turn this into an active hub. The power adapter to do so is NOT included.

Unlike the single-speed original version, this has a knob so you can vary the speed. It's not precise, but there is a somewhat noticeable difference between low and high. It's a continually variable speed - you can turn the dial to whatever speed you like.

Best of all, it's just as quiet, if not quieter, than the original model. That's the biggest plus for me by far, since the cheap USB fans make a racket. This just makes a low-pitched hum. The build quality is solid - the base is sturdy, and the bendable arm holds its position well.

One negative: the packaging. It's in a clam shell package that is a major, major pain to open!

While it's more expensive than the original, the added benefits of being able to position it on a desk and use it as a hub makes the upgrade worth considering. Highly recommend.

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>USA EDITION:
I've have (and use) a couple other Arctic USB fans and have been 100% satisfied with them. This new version (their "USA Edition") has a couple of improvements over past designs.

The base is a metal plate which increases the fan's stability when you're bending the stem to point the fan. The on/off/speed dial switch no longer has a lit LED ring around it. I never found the lit LED ring to be bothersome on the other Arctic fans, so having or not having it is not a big deal to me.

The base also does away with the USB hub connections that other models have. That's keeps the base more streamlined and allows it to have a lower profile. It also does away with the clam shell packaging, instead using a very easy to open box.

The build quality of this, like the other Arctic fans I have, is excellent. The stem is bendy by stays put where you want it; the operating sound is pretty hushed; the on/off/speed control works well. The overall design is attractive, with a red/white/blue color scheme and graphics.

It moves a surprising amount of air. No, it won't blow your hair back as a Vornado fan will, but this makes a noticeable difference in circulating air. The size makes it very easy to find a spot on your desk to position it.

While I can't speak to the long-term reliability of this as of yet, I expect it will last for some time. I have an Arctic fan similar to this that I've been using almost daily for the past 1+ years, and it still works as good as it did when new.

Looks good, works well, and easy to use. Highly recommend.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: ARCTIC Breeze Pro USB Desktop Fan with 4-Port USB Hub

TomTom XXL 550 5-Inch Portable GPS Navigator (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I am pleased with the overall performance of the TomTom XXL 550T. It's not perfect but the good points outweigh the bad, and I would recommend this product. Below are a summary of the good and not so good points:

Great features:
* Large screen; easy to read while driving
* Can switch between 2D and 3D display with the touch of the screen
* Accurate maps which include many small side streets - not just the main roads
* Cross-streets are labeled with their names on the 3D map which lets you see what's coming up next
* Convenient plug-in with long cord to your car's 12 volt power supply
* Easy to program your route
* Able to download map updates from the Internet
* Display includes your speed and the speed limit (Unit will even alert you if you exceed the speed limit by 5 mph)
* Fun feature: Can select the type of car to display to represent your car on the maps

Features that could be improved:
* Hard to position unit with the suction cup mount without the unit snapping out of the mount assembly (Which is the main reason I rated this 3 stars for ease of use.)
* USB cable to connect to the computer was hard to connect (had a strange angle)
* Not able to program "auto-dim" of the screen (You have to manually switch between daytime and nightime mode)
* Map graphics aren't realistic - look like a cartoon drawing
* Had an issue with prior routes being held and highlighted in red on the map display

I've had good luck on trips with this TomTom and in spite of some minor flaws, I think it's a reliable, easy to program GPS.
text_fidelity_b: TomTom XXL 550 5-Inch Portable GPS Navigator (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
VIZIO Sound Bar for TV, 28” 2.1 Surround Sound System for TV with Wireless Subwoofer and Bluetooth, Channel Home Theater Sound Bar – Remote SB2821-D6 The first delivery had subwoofer that was dead on arrival. No power.

They sent a replacement. It works great. Music streaming from my phone or computer by bluetooth sounds great. Better than my Bose.

If you want instruction on how to operate this thing properly look at the copied review below. This was helpful.

One other or two were somewhat helpful.

The instructions they put in the package gets the thing on but doesn't tell you how to operate it.

FYI:

"Please handle this unit with care when taking it out of the box. The sub-woofer in particular, which has the speaker cone located on the bottom of the sub-woofer. If you grab it from the bottom, you could damage it very easily. When set up properly, I found this Sound Bar to have very good sound. However it did take me awhile to reach this state. Because like most men, I know everything, I skipped through the instructions, plugged in the sound bar and was extremely disappointed in the quality of the sound. Here are a few tips to make things easier. If you're doing a horizontal installation in front of the TV at ear level, the sound button the the bar should be located on top, and the small lights that show volume level, etc., should be located on the left when facing your TV. That way the speakers are facing you. Also, I had a difficult time finding the audio settings on my TV to turn off the internal speakers and use the external speakers. Naturally I thought, heck just turn down the volume on the TV speakers to zero and it should be the same thing. Wrong !! You have to find and turn on the external speakers, and turn off the internal speakers for this sound bar to work properly. The sound bar does come with a remote, which is an absolute necessity no matter which sound bar you order. Read the instruction manual carefully, as you have to use the 'previous" and "next" buttons to adjust the Sub-woofer, Bass and Treble settings. Since I know everything, I naturally assumed the volume up and down buttons would adjust these settings. Wrong !! Also, there are buttons to enable TruVolume, and TruSurround HD, but the manual doesn't clarify exactly when to use these settings or what they actually do. I suggest trying both settings and see if you notice any difference in sound quality. I've read a few complaints about the bass not being that strong, but I found it to be excellent. I wonder if these users had the sub-woofer in the correct location, and if they figured out how to raise the sub-woofer level using the remote, and if the sub-woofer stopped working and needed to be "re-linked". I had to re-link mine, and although the instructions could be better, got the sub-woofer working properly in a few minutes. With the sub-woofer is turned on, located in the right area, and adjusted with the remote, you should be very happy with the results. Why only 4 stars for this product? First, the instruction manual could have been more informative about the settings on the remote, and second the ergonomics of the remote are in my opinion very bad. The volume adjustment in particular is usually an up and down toggle on every remote I ever used, but not on this one. The technical designer genius of this remote decided to put a big square "enter/play/pause button between the up and down volume adjustment buttons. Hence adjusting the volume by feel is the worst of any remote I've ever had. That being said, once set up properly, you should be extremely happy with the sound quality of this sound bar."
text_fidelity_b: VIZIO Sound Bar for TV, 28” 2.1 Surround Sound System for TV with Wireless Subwoofer and Bluetooth, Channel Home Theater Sound Bar – Remote SB2821-D6

text_fidelity_a:
Panasonic SC-BTT195 Energy Star 5.1-Channel 1000-Watt Full HD 3D Blu-Ray Home Theater System with Tall Boy Speakers Good sound for the money and does what I expected. Skip to the summation if you are looking for reasons not to purchase.

Might be a better choice especially if you own a Panasonic TV as the set up is designed for a Panasonic product line. I had to use their support call service a few times and as most companies today, some are very good and can understand and help, but most will read a prewritten script and hope they hit on the problem you are experiencing. Cons: Had to go buy after market speaker wires due to the lack of length that comes with the system and splice the wires to place the rear speakers. Also had to buy an audio connector to allow the system to produce TV sound. This really ticked me off and Panasonic should really step up and correct these issues. The system also needs to modernize and add another HDMI connection ( and the cable ...really? ) to allow for a cleaner install. Another con is the system will not produce sound while watching the Internet based VUDU movie channel. Panasonic wanted me to buy another movie and call them to "try" some fixes while the movie played! It does work with my cable provided paid movie service. The system would also not work with my top of the line wireless router and had to buy a cable and run wires to their system. One must also buy another adapter ( Dingle) to receive wireless signals that may or may not work or a connecting cable. Check to see see the distance from your router to the system and if it is physically possible to fish the wire to the sound system from the router before you buy the cable.

Summation: "You get what you pay for". If you can splice wires and figure out how to add cables to make TV audio work and the internet work then it's ok. You will need to spend more money on items that should be included from Panasonic and it is best to own a newer Panasonic TV for easier installation. Panasonic kind of ruined what should be a great experience by cutting corners to save money on wire and connections. Panasonic should provide more installation on information "needs" as part of their product description if they aren't not going to provide long enough speaker wire, HDMI connectors and inputs,or audio cables,or internet Dingle or cable.
text_fidelity_b: Panasonic SC-BTT195 Energy Star 5.1-Channel 1000-Watt Full HD 3D Blu-Ray Home Theater System with Tall Boy Speakers

Zmodo 1080p HD NVR WiFi System 4 HD Outdoor and 4 HD Indoor 1.0 Megapixel Wide Angle Wireless Security Camera with 500GB Hard Drive, Intelligent Recording, Smart Motion Detection, Web Access We have been using our 8cam setup for over a month and we are very happy with this purchase. The cameras were purchased to help us get our pre teen back on track. He recently got himself in trouble and we set these cameras up all over the house and eventually outside to keep our child honest.

Not only did it turn our sons behavior right around, but we now have an awesome setup to monitor our house when we are not around.

Although the software was not exactly very explanatory, I will pass along some of our learnings.

The software occasionally fails to give updates on alarms but resetting the phone seems to fix this right away. You do not have to purchase their cloud software to view the cameras: just plug an HDMI cable into the NVR and a mouse and you are set to view all the motion detections and recordings. I like how the cameras are not 1080p but are 720p. This gives our 500gb hard drive a break and we can record over a month on the NVR before overwriting data.

The NVR software was easy you setup and runs completely off of the device. The cameras were easy to setup and were plug and play.

I will eventually setup my router to port forward so I can remote into the recordings at any time although I don't think that will be necessary for our needs. I love the free alerts and its great to get the notifications on the phone to alert you of motion detected!

All in all this product was fantastic for what we needed and you can not beat the bundle price for the 500gb hard drove and 8 cameras! Thanks!

text_fidelity_a:
Sony Digital Flash Voice Recorder (ICD-PX312) This was bought to replace a tape unit to record class lectures for about $50. It is was a major upgrade. It's compact. When you can make recordings they come with a date and time in the file info which makes sorting them much easier. You can also record in to different folders, though you can only edit the folder names on a computer. I have also used this with an external microphone, with which it also worked well.

I use this recorder with NIMH batteries, but it doesn't seem to like them given how it stops recording when the charge of the batteries drops to 40% (tested separately afterwards). I guess this is really meant to be used with alkaline batteries. When the unit quit in class, which I could tell because it beeps when it turns off, I reached for my cell phone. Listening to the cell phone recording afterwards and comparing it to this device I can tell that the cell phone records with background noise and at low sensitivity. text_fidelity_a:
Garmin 010-01689-00 Forerunner 35; Easy-to-Use GPS Running Watch, Black I did a good amount of research on other devices before buying this product. I initially wanted a sleek smartwatch that also had great fitness tracking modes, but apparently you either get a pretty smartwatch/OK fitness tracker, or a decent fitness tracker/outdated looking smartwatch. In the end I decided I wanted mainly a fitness tracker that has some smartwatch features, and that I wouldn't use most of the features on an actual smartwatch.

PROS

The app is awesome! My husband is a software developer so I learn a lot about what makes good apps good and what makes bad apps bad. This app is free and user friendly. It has mostly accurate measurements and you can easily track your progress and areas of improvement. It also has a feature that allows whoever you send the link to to track your location, in case you are concerned about getting kidnapped on your run. Very good stuff.

The steps I get seem to be pretty consistent as well as the distance traveled. The heartrate tracker seems to be mostly accurate (checked with manual pulse check).

The battery life is pretty good. Obviously I would use more battery if I am using the fitness modes. Depending on your activity level and use of the fitness modes, the battery could last you all week plus some. The battery charges to full in about 30 minutes.

I like the rectangular watch face and the light green band. I also like that you can change the bands. Apparently for some of the expensive FitBit models the band is not changeable so some people just buy a whole new watch. Like whaaat?

CONS
I like being able to see the texts I get on the watch, but I don't really care for receiving phone calls (I get so many spam calls that I don't even answer my phone lol). I don't think there is a way to say 'no' to having phone calls, so I get frequent notifications to enable phone call permissions. It's not too much of a problem but it's kind of annoying sometimes.

I think the sleep tracker is interesting, but I don't think it is accurate. I think that as long as you are "resting" during the hours that you put as your sleeping hours under Settings, that it considers this as sleep. Sometimes I can't sleep but the device considers this as light sleep. I think this would be an interesting addition, that perhaps it could be integrated: I am a night shift worker and I switch between day/night sleep, so I have to manually enter my bedtimes in the app's User Settings to sleep. I think that if there was an activity button, like when you choose walk/run/cardio on the watch itself, for sleep, it would be easier for me personally. I am not sure if that could be done with a software update or if this is a hardware type thing.

FINAL THOUGHTS

I wear this watch almost 24/7 and I think it has helped me consider and evaluate my activity levels as well as track my improvement. I think that if Garmin made a watch that had the aesthetics and watch interface comparable to the Apple watch but kept the good fitness aspect, I would definitely purchase as an upgrade.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin 010-01689-00 Forerunner 35; Easy-to-Use GPS Running Watch, Black

text_fidelity_a:
ARCTIC P402BT Bluetooth Stereo Headphones with Integrated Mic, A2DP/AVRCP, 30-Hour Playback for Tablet/Smartphone/MP3 - Black These are pretty good bluetooth headphones. They excel with regard to comfort - the ear padding is plush and they have a nice balance between grip (e.g., staying put when you move) and comfort. The headband consists of 2 plastic rods without any padding, but doesn't cause a significant comfort issue.

I had zero problems pairing these with a couple of different tablets (Android operating system and the Fire version of Android). Simple, quick and painless. The operating range is also excellent, with zero dropouts at about 20 feet and only minor dropouts at 25+ feet.

The sound quality is quite good. While these open-ear designs don't have the booming bass quality of closed designs, I found the sound quality to be very good, especially in the midrange. They are an excellent choice for movie watching since the dialogue comes through so clearly.

I like the operating controls, especially the volume switch. It's a rocker-type design, so it's very easy to use without having to look at the button - just find it by feel, and press up to increase volume and down to decrease. The multifunction button is in the middle of the rocker switch and is very easy to find by touch as well.

The overall look is very snazzy, and the build quality appears solid.

There is only a modest amount of sound isolation, but that again is an issue inherent with open-ear headphones. It does cut ambient sound reasonably well - I had no problems listening to music while on a noisy treadmill without the ambient sound interfering to any significant degree.

Misses are the volume level. These have a rather limited upper volume range. Normally I set my tablet to about the 75% level and the headphone level to close to the upper point to get a good volume that blocks out ambient noise. With these, however, I had to set the tablet sound level to 100% and the earphone level also at 100%, and I still found them a bit lacking in volume. Given the price point, the range should be better.

But other than the volume issue, no complaints. Good sound, good comfort, great range and easy-to-use controls. Well worth considering.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: ARCTIC P402BT Bluetooth Stereo Headphones with Integrated Mic, A2DP/AVRCP, 30-Hour Playback for Tablet/Smartphone/MP3 - Black

Western Digital 320GB WD Black Performance Mobile Hard Drive - 7200 RPM Class, SATA 6 Gb/s, , 32 MB Cache, 2.5" - WD3200LPLX Update 8-7-19: I went to the WD website to register my two drives. They show as no warranty from WD, presumably because they were bought through a reseller. Just so you know ...

I use these as primary storage (and backup storage) for our MacBook Air laptop. Most MacBooks now come with solid state drives, meaning memory chip based drives, not physical spinning disks. They are much more expensive than the heritage physical disk approach, such that the largest SSD that we could get with our 2017 MacBook Air was a 256 GB drive. These WD Black (virtually enterprise level) drives are 500 GB each, so our storage is 2x that of the built in drive. We use one as our primary external drive; once a month we install the 2nd drive (also externally), copy the files across, and put it into our safe deposit box at the bank. If we ever lose a drive, whether to failure or someone breaking in and stealing our drive and laptop, we're only 30 days behind, a real advantage.

The only downside to this drive is that the warranty on the drive itself is provided by the Seller, OEMGENUINE. The drive came marked with a label on the drive as a Seller 5 year warranty, with no terms provided. The downside risk is there is no published warranty, either by the Seller or by WD on their website, and whatever warranty is provided is subject to the Seller still being in existence over the next 5 years. However, given the price of the drive ($35 or so), it was a reasonable risk to take, especially since we acquired two and use one as the backup to the primary one. The odds of losing two drives at the same time is pretty remote. So we accepted the risk, but dropped the review for the product & seller by 1 star. If you go to the WD website, they do claim a 5 year limited warranty. I am a little surprised that the WD website doesn't provide a link to their warranty. So if we can't reach OEMGENUINE should we have a problem, I'm not sure what protection we'll have from WD. Something to consider if that's important to you.

These are fast drives (7200 rpm for the 500GB drive), which is noticeably faster than the previous bulk drives we've purchased online and/or removed from existing systems, which have all been 5400 rpm drives. SATA compatible, plug and play, no issues yet but it's only been a few days. If something materially changes, I'll post an update.
text_fidelity_b: Western Digital 320GB WD Black Performance Mobile Hard Drive - 7200 RPM Class, SATA 6 Gb/s, , 32 MB Cache, 2.5" - WD3200LPLX

I thought when I got this surge suppressor that the extension cord was meant to be used with it so you'd have a total of nine feet of cord if needed. Apparently, the extension cord doesn't actually fit the surge suppressor; the extension cord has three two-prong receptacles that you could plug, say, lamps and the like into, but you cannot plug the surge suppressor itself into it. The extension cord is clearly marked as being for two-wire polarized, as opposed to three-prong grounded, appliances. So that's more than a little misleading.

The surge suppressor looks heavy-duty, but you are cautioned in the packaging literature that it's not to be used with "sensitive equipment" like everything we use surge suppressors for: computers, TV, etc. You can't use it with things involving water, either, like aquariums. So what would I use it for? A blow dryer? I think not. To make it even worse, you are told to cover the receptacles on the extension cord if they are not in use. There are little plastic sliders that you're supposed to use for this purpose. But one of the sliders on the extension cord I received won't stay closed. China-cheap.

Belkin has some good products, but this one doesn't impress me very much. And the whole thing is packaged in one of those awful clamshells that you risk hurting yourself on when you take the scissors to it.

text_fidelity_a:
Surge Protector Power Strip with USB, Silicone Extension Cord with 10 Outlets 3 USB Charging Ports and 1 USB-C Charging Port, 1875W/15A Overload Surge Protection, Gift for Mother's Day PROS

1. It has 10 sockets/outlets.
2. Two of the sockets are offset from the other six. This allows them to be used for wide plugs, which is an important feature, because wide plugs are a frequent occurrence on appliances.
3. The color is an attractive but neutral black which makes the strip fade into the background more than the strips I own which are white or beige.
4. In addition to being a power strip, it also provides surge protection.
5. There are four USB ports that can be used for charging devices. One of them is a USB-C port and the other 3 are standard USB ports. The manufacturer claims in the manual that the three standard USB ports are “smart” USB ports.

CONS

1. I am not entirely comfortable trusting the “smart” USB ports on this device for charging. I feel more comfortable using a regular USB charging adapter and plugging it into a socket on the surge protector side of this device.

2. Regarding the smart USB ports, there are not adequate instructions either in the manual or on the manufacturer’s website that clearly explain the implications of this feature and how to utilize it. I cannot find information on the top mA it supports in charging.

GENERAL INFORMATION ON USB CHARGING

In order to test this device for my Vine review, I spent over two hours (!!!) trying to find comprehensible information on what the term “smart” means in the context of a USB port on a power strip like this one. Unfortunately, I was left with more questions than answers, for which hassle I’m dropping a star off this review. I’ve included some of what I learned below, for what it might be worth to any fellow Amazon customer who might be thinking of purchasing this product.

A smart USB charger port supposedly can, in and of itself, figure out what the optimal charging speed of a specific device is when it is plugged into that port, in order to neither overload it with too much current or under-deliver to it the optimal current. The question on everyone’s mind these days (it certainly has been on mine), is whether it is possible to destroy the battery in a particular device by slamming too much current into it. Apparently, the answer to this all-important question is: No. If, for example, you take a phone which comes with a 900mA wall charger, and you plug it into a 2,100mA charger that comes with a different device you own, it will not damage the phone. It will only speed up the length of time it takes for the phone’s battery to charge. However, if you have a USB device older than 2007, it may not charge on any USB ports newer than the (now ancient), 500mA USB 1.0 and 2.0 PC ports. Which means such older devices may not charge even on the “smart” USB ports on this device.

USB charging current is measured in mA (milliampere, 1/1000 of an ampere, the basic unit for measuring electrical current). There are three kinds of USB ports which are defined by their current specs: a standard downstream port, a charging downstream port, and a dedicated charging port. The first two are found on a desktop computer. The third kind is a “dumb” wall charger.

USB 1.0 and 2.0 standard downstream ports on a computer can deliver up to 500mA (0.5A).

USB 3.0 standard downstream ports on a computer can deliver up to 900mA (0.9A).

USB 3.1 and USB 3.2 ports can deliver between 1,500mA (1.5A) and 3,000mA (3A).

Charging downstream USB ports on a computer can deliver up to 1,500mA (1.5A).

Dedicated USB charging ports on a computer can deliver up to 3,000mA (3A).
text_fidelity_b: Surge Protector Power Strip with USB, Silicone Extension Cord with 10 Outlets 3 USB Charging Ports and 1 USB-C Charging Port, 1875W/15A Overload Surge Protection, Gift for Mother's Day

Lenovo IdeaPad Gaming 3 - (2022) - Essential Gaming Laptop Computer - 15.6" FHD - 120Hz - AMD Ryzen 5 6600H - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 - 8GB DDR5 RAM - 256GB NVMe Storage - Windows 11 Home I’ve spent the last month using and playing games on the Lenovo IdeaPad Gaming 3. It’s a decent entry-level laptop. I wouldn’t consider it a dedicated gaming machine, but more aimed at daily use plus some gaming.

The laptop includes 3 free months of Xbox Game Pass, so I’ve played games available through that library. Games like Moonlighter, Moonglow Bay, Tunic, Sims 4, and Hades. The laptop handled all of those just fine, but many are older games and/or not very hardware intensive.

However, I don’t think 8GB of RAM and a 256GB SSD are enough. In my very first day of downloading games, I filled more than half the hard drive (and only ~236GB is available to start). As for the RAM, my 5-year-old laptop has 8GB of RAM and I’m feeling it. A laptop from 2022 should start with at least 16GB.

The Quad Vent fans vent in the back and on both sides of the laptop. I wish there wasn’t a vent on the right, because it’s right where the mouse sits. After maybe twenty to thirty minutes, my hand gets sweaty, which isn’t great when playing a competitive game.

There are 2 USB-A ports, one on each side. The back has an HDMI port, Ethernet, USB-C, and the power input. I actually really like the power input being on the back, as that way the cable isn’t in the way when using the mouse. But I’d like another USB-A port in the back, because I can see using a hub with this laptop.

The keyboard is not my favorite. On the plus side, it’s a full keyboard. I can’t remember the last time I saw a laptop with a numpad. The keyboard has backlighting, but only one color option: white. The keys are flat on top and somewhat slippery. The keyboard itself feels cramped, especially when gaming with WASD.

The laptop is heavy, about 7 or 8 pounds. It’s not something you’ll want to tote from class to class. The battery lasts about an hour if playing games, and about 3 hours for normal use.
text_fidelity_b: Lenovo IdeaPad Gaming 3 - (2022) - Essential Gaming Laptop Computer - 15.6" FHD - 120Hz - AMD Ryzen 5 6600H - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 - 8GB DDR5 RAM - 256GB NVMe Storage - Windows 11 Home

XPPen Artist12 Pro 11.6 Inch Drawing Monitor Pen Display Full-Laminated Graphics Drawing Tablet with Tilt Function Battery-Free Stylus and 8 Shortcut Keys(8192 Levels Pen Pressure and 72% NTSC) I'm a seasoned designer and have been working on expanding my skill set in illustration and pattern design. My search for a drawing tablet has been a little bumpy. I started with the iPad Pro, and dropped a big chunk of change on it feeling confident I would love it. I wanted to use it with AstroPad so I could draw in Adobe Illustrator via my laptop, like a regular drawing tablet. Unfortunately, I hated the experience - the Astropad connection wasn't smooth enough for me and most importantly, the feeling of the Apple Pencil against the iPad glass made my skin crawl. I thought I would get used to it, but I never did, and my iPad ended up collecting dust.

So I started looking into dedicated graphics tablets. I initially bought one from a different brand. It was a model that didn't have a display screen. I really liked the way that one felt; worlds better than the iPad. But the drivers for that one were super buggy and unreliable. So I sent that one back too.

Finally, I decided to take a chance on the XP-Pen Artist 13.3 Pro and I am SO glad I did! The instructions for installing and setting up the drivers & controls were on the website and super clear (I'm on a Mac running Mojave). I was able to easily map all the buttons to the controls I wanted in Illustrator, and I was happily drawing no more than 40 minutes after opening the box.

I've been using this tablet for a few days now and it's been smooth sailing. The display is big and beautiful and there's no lag. The screen feels great to draw on. Not exactly "like paper" as some have said, but it definitely feels nice. Nice glide but with just enough resistance to feel like an authentic drawing experience.

I am very happy with this purchase.

PROS:
• Display is big and beautiful
• Zero lag
• Pen feels great on the screen
• Easy to set up
• Comes with lots of accessories

Cons:
• The 3-in-1 cable works great but feels bulky, especially if you are using the tablet anywhere other than a desk. But that's just what wires are like, I suppose. For me, the tradeoff is worth it b/c wires mean there's never any lag or connectivity issues.

• It was a pain to find a case for this. I wish XP-Pen made one for this size tablet. I ended up purchasing this one and it's worked out well: https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B07JC8MZH1/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_asin_title_o01_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1
text_fidelity_b: XPPen Artist12 Pro 11.6 Inch Drawing Monitor Pen Display Full-Laminated Graphics Drawing Tablet with Tilt Function Battery-Free Stylus and 8 Shortcut Keys(8192 Levels Pen Pressure and 72% NTSC)

In interim, HD video streaming, surfing, gaming etc..all work flawlessly.

Comments for WD PowerLine owners:
1. WD utility is unable to pickup on speed of the TP-Links (Rate Mbps). This is an application issue obviously and not completely sure if I can get around this as of yet.
2. I have not secured or modified network name as of yet which made things easier. Hope this does work when I get to it.

For everyone:
My WD PowerLines were collecting dust until I moved. My previous home had a different circuit setup that prevented any PowerLine units from working correctly. They would see each other, but speeds were like dialup. So, don't be ticked if these do not work.

My new house has limited drops and roughly 3k Sq Ft over 2 floors and have no issues. My WD's have over 160 Mbps indicated on the utility from top to bottom.

Trying an Anker brand cable and if it can't last at least a year I'm done with aux cables, I'll upgrade to Grom bluetooth.

SanDisk Ultra Fit 128GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive - SDCZ43-128G-GAM46 I've always been really happy with SanDisk cards and flash drives, both for speed and reliability, unhesitatingly recommending them vs playing data roulette with generic drives. So I didn't really think twice when I needed to upgrade to a 128GB flashdrive from my smaller ones, I just ordered another SanDisk Ultra Fit.
Oops. No more.
The many other reviews are correct. This drive has serious overheating problems.
It works great if you're not trying to write more than a few GB at a time.
It also works pretty well in an external USB Hub, wrapped in ice packs. But that's not exactly practical, and completely defeats the purpose of getting a small form factor drive in the first place.
It also works okay if I intentionally throttle data transfer 30%-50%, but that's really pretty pointless, isn't it?
So it's not bad for storing data, photos, video, etc., as long as you don't mind setting up ice packs for the initial loading. But useless for backups, hosting virtual machines, sneaker net, or any other data intensive operation.
Basically useless for at least half of what I wanted it for.
And SanDisk's generic response "SanDisk drives comply with industry specific standards and are tested to remain in acceptable temperature ranges under normal operating conditions" is pretty darn useless too.
[Edit] Be aware that when it overheats it starts randomly disconnecting. This will corrupt datafiles being written ***without any warning***. If you care about your data, you need to do a CRC or full binary compare after copying data to this drive.
text_fidelity_b: SanDisk Ultra Fit 128GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive - SDCZ43-128G-GAM46

text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Fire HD 8 tablet, 8” HD Display, 32 GB, 30% faster processor, designed for portable entertainment, (2022 release), Rose TL;DR

The Kindle Fire HD 8 is a serviceable tablet if you don’t intend to use it for much outside of consuming media, primarily from Amazon’s in-house apps. If you’re interested, I recommend that you wait until they’re on sale before making the purchase.

Full Review:

I bought my Kindle Fire HD 8 primarily for listening to music. I use Amazon Music (Unlimited subscriber) and it has a headphone jack. Not wanting to deal with the ads from the lockscreen, I paid to have them removed. Over the past few weeks, I’ve been playing around with the device to see what it’s capable of when it comes to media consumption. Here’s what I’ve come up with! I did manage to sideload Google Play and several apps. I’ll reflect on those experiences, though any issues I had from this will not count against the device, as Google Play and the apps from it are not officially supported.

Interface and Build Quality
You are pretty much stuck with their stock interface. You can’t remove ANY of the Amazon apps from the homescreen. However, you can hide them away in a folder. This cleaned things up, nicely. Toward the top of the screen, you have a static bar that shows your last 2 apps, as well as some recommended apps. They do manage to sneak a sponsored app in there from time to time. Seeing that I paid to get rid of ads, this annoyed me (though it really doesn’t impact my use.) I actually like typing on this more than I do my Samsung Galaxy Tab S6 Lite or my Samsung S22 phone, which surprised me. One would think they’d make sure their own apps are working on their own devices at least as well as the apps work on their competitors devices.

The tablet itself feels kinda cheap, but not as cheap as I expected. The screen’s glass isn’t as smooth as my Samsung devices, but it’s quite functional. You can tell there’s not much power under the hood, as apps take a few seconds to load, and there’s sometimes interface lag when interacting with them. The onboard speakers suck, but I don’t use them. Headphones are the way to go… and since it has a headphone jack, I’m all set. The display is plenty for what I use it for.

Support
I’ve reached out to Amazon a few times to ask questions, or to get help. They’ve been incredibly responsive. The reps have always been courteous and informative. High marks here!

Audio and Video Quality
Music sounds great through my Audio Technica ATH-M50x headphones, especially HD and Ultra HD from Amazon Music. Strangely, the app does not have an EQ option (I can adjust the EQ on my Windows PC and on my other Android devices.) It supports my Fosi Audio DS1 with no problems. This improves the sound a bit (mostly making things a bit louder.) It did not power up my Fosi Audio K5 Pro, however. Unfortunately, the Kindle Fire HD 8 did not support my Bluetooth Audio Technica ATH-SR50BT’s, which was a disappointment. On the flipside, I was able to sideload 4Stream and the Andover Songbird app to get it to stream HD audio to my Denon D-M41, which was a pleasant surprise.

I took some time to watch some streaming video via Prime Video, Netflix and YouTube (sideloaded via Google Play.) Even though it’s not a true “HD” display, the screen is small enough to make it not matter so much. Lord of the Rings - Fellowship of the Rings probably benefited from this, as the movie didn’t age well in our HD world. The audio on it was also quite engaging through my headphones. Ash vs the Evil Dead on Netflix also streamed flawlessly, and looked great on the screen. YouTube videos play just fine as well, even though the app was sideloaded.

As an eReader
The Kindle Fire HD 8 works great as an eReader, as one would expect. Since I don’t plan to read much from it, I didn’t explore it much. Books loaded just fine, and you can interact with them as you’d expect (the Kindle is pretty robust for this, for those who’re interested.)

Non-media Consumption
I tried getting Discord to work on the Fire HD 8. While I was able to install it, the experience was pretty terrible. Browsing the internet with the Silk browser leaves some to be desired, and the mail/calendar apps are not something I’m interested in using. Again, I’m using this primarily for music, so I’m fine with this. However, if I needed to use it for anything productive, I’d be quite frustrated.

Google Play
Instructions on how to get Google Play installed are readily available online, and it’s easily doable within an hour’s time. I was able to install an EQ for my music, which works okay (I did have the app crash once.) The Gmail app loaded fairly well, as did Google Chrome. However, I can’t sync Chrome, as my email account was already used to activate the Kindle. There haven’t been any issues with YouTube. Dragon Quest 1 and 2 installed flawlessly and seem to work fine. However, Baldur’s Gate 1 & 2, along with other Beamdog games did not install at all (these aren’t officially supported, but folks claim it works. Not for me!) Again, none of these experiences with Google Play will count for or against my overall rating for this device. I’m simply stating them in case anyone else is interested in tinkering.

Ultimately, the Kindle Fire HD 8 is okay for the money (when on sale.) It works for my purposes, but I can tell it’d leave a lot to be desired if I wanted to use it for anything more. The fact that they still advertise apps on the home screen, even after you pay to remove ads is annoying (enough to knock my rating down a star.) I do suspect that the Kindle Fire devices are probably loss-leaders, and any ads they can cram in help generate income.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Fire HD 8 tablet, 8” HD Display, 32 GB, 30% faster processor, designed for portable entertainment, (2022 release), Rose

text_fidelity_a:
KZ ZS10 Pro, Linsoul 4BA+1DD 5 Driver in Ear Monitor, HiFi Metal Earphones, with Stainless Steel Faceplate, 2 Pin Detachable Cable (Without Mic, Black) Best sounding in-ear headphones I've ever heard, by a mile. I've owned the Bang and Olufsen H3, Sony XBA H1, Klipsch S4, X7, X6i, 1More Dual Drivers, Beats by Dr Dre Tour (wired), and Monster Cable's Jamz and Turbines.

The bass has lots of range and goes DEEP, in some tracks it even reminds me of my Kicker CVR 12' car subwoofer I used to blast about 15 years ago. It is not quite that overpowering, of course, and it balances out nicely with the other frequencies. The midrange is very present and natural sounding judging by how vocals and guitar strings sound. The highs are beautiful, they sound very accurate to me and present no sibilance. The overall sound is very rich and detailed, it allows you to follow specific instruments as you listen, and it even presents some soundstage (which I didn't think was possible in in-ears, maybe my aforementioned B&O H3 had some)

Overall these do have a V sound signature with boosted bass and treble, but not as marked as almost everything else that's in the market. In order to eliminate any fatigue caused by this, I would strongly recommend that you disable any bass boost, make sure you're not elevating bass or treble at all in EQ, and go even deeper and disable default features like Dolby Atmos (Oneplus phone) and even the Hi Fi quad DAC on LG phones (which I've found does introduce a bit of a V curve itself)

Other than their sound these earphones' build quality seems very good and durable. I'm in disbelief they could cost $60. You're welcome
text_fidelity_b: KZ ZS10 Pro, Linsoul 4BA+1DD 5 Driver in Ear Monitor, HiFi Metal Earphones, with Stainless Steel Faceplate, 2 Pin Detachable Cable (Without Mic, Black)

OCTA Spider Monkey - Secure Height Adjustable Stand for iPad, Galaxy, Surface and All Tablets for Desk, Bed, Car, Couch Do I like the Spider Monkey? Yes... with reservations. First let me cover why I like it. I read in bed, and I spend a lot of time switching hands, trying to find ways to prop my book or tablet up, shaking feeling back into my fingers. And then, when I fall asleep, which I always do, the tablet might end up under me or might end up on the floor, and neither is good. The Spider Monkey gives me a way to prop up my tablet without holding it, and to keep it out of my way when I fall asleep.

The downside? How it works depends very much on what you attach it to. I have a headboard that allows me to twist and anchor the tail in a lot of ways, but it doesn't always hold the tablet in position. It can swing around, and be difficult to angle for good reading. Also? It's not all that easy to put together. Once you do, it'll hold, but until then you may find yourself screaming in frustration.

In spite of the drawbacks, though, the Spider Monkey has been a real boon to my reading. If I work with it a bit, it'll even hold my kindle in its cover. I'm not sure I think it's worth $80, to be honest. Half that seems fair to me.

Disclaimer: I received this product in exchange for an honest review.

text_fidelity_a:
SanDisk iXpand 16GB Mobile Flash Drive with Lightning Connector for iPhones, iPads & Computers (SDIX-016G-G57) I bought this because I was traveling abroad and I wanted to backup my phone pictures. If my phone got lost or stolen on the last day of the trip, I would lose all my pictures from the entire trip. It's definitely better to backup your pictures each evening so they most you could ever lose would be the pictures from 1 day. You would still have the rest.

This is mostly just an issue when traveling abroad. Back home where WiFi is common, the iCloud backup is just fine. Unless you take zillions of pictures, you can even use your cell data to backup your pictures when there's no WiFi (assuming you have a reasonable data plan). However, when traveling abroad or on a cruise, access to the cloud can be quite expensive and/or limited. That's where this device comes in handy. Backup your pictures without WiFi or cell data.

There is another reason why you might want this device. If you take tons of pictures on your phone, then space can be a problem. You might be running out of space on your phone and/or the cloud. Or maybe you don't have an iCloud account at all. You want to make room on your phone, but you also want to keep all the pictures. You can copy your pictures to this device, and delete them off the phone to make room for more pictures.

The concept of backup up pictures from your phone is a good one, but I don't think this device is the best way to do it. I just bought the RAVPower FileHub wireless travel router, SD card reader, USB portable drive companion. I think that's going to end up being a better solution than this device.

There are a couple of things I don't like about this device:
1) The drive is very wide. If you have two USB ports that are close to each other, the drive will block the other port.
2) I find the connection to the iPhone to be awkward. The lightning connector on the device is on the end of this flexible rubber arm on the side of the device. You bend this arm away from the device (but not too far, per the warning in the instructions), and plug it into the phone. It's hard to describe, but you end up with this thing at an awkward angle hanging off the bottom of the phone. You wouldn't want to put it in your pocket like that, and it sits funny on the table since both the phone and the device are at an angle. If you flip the device around, you can get the phone to lay flat on the table, but then the device is blocking the home button. It's a really goofy design.
3) This last one takes a while to explain. There is a sync mode, where you can automatically sync the device with your phone. This will save any new pictures from your phone onto the drive. Here's how it works: You run the app, plug the device into the lightning connector, and run the sync. Pictures are copied to a folder on the drive that you specify. Since you create the folder originally, and you associate the phone's sync with that folder, you can use the device with multiple phones. Simply use a different folder for each phone. When you sync, any new pictures on the phone which aren't already in the sync folder will be copied to the drive. The concept is very good.

However, one huge drawback of the sync is that the file named aren't preserved. For example, if you just copy a picture off your phone using some other method, you'll get something like "IMG_2841". That's an easy name to deal with, if you want to do something with a particular picture (e.g. Bob wants a copy of IMG_1531, or I want to print an 8x10 of IMG_2316).

Unfortunately, when you use the sync method, the file names are not preserved. The picture files get really long names with a seemingly random string of characters. I'm sure the names mean something to the sync program, but for a human they just look like random garbage. In any case, your drive ends up with this sync folder filled with hundreds (or thousands) of files with random unreadable names. If you want to do anything with the files, you'll wish they had more recognizable names.

Let's say for example that you copied IMG_1000 and IMG_1001 off your phone using some other method, and later you decide you also want IMG_1002. Well, you know that the picture must be in the sync folder, but good luck finding it. You wish you could just sort by name and grab IMG_1002 directly, but since the names are all random you'll need to scroll through hundreds (or thousands) of thumbnails and try to figure out which picture was originally called IMG_1002.

Because of this issue, I think the sync mode is useless.

However, you can still back up your pictures in a semi-manual way. The trick is that if you do a manual copy to get a picture from the phone onto the drive, then the original file name is preserved. So, instead of doing the sync, use the manual copy mode. This isn't quite as tedious as it sounds because the app understands the problem with duplicate file names, and it gives you the opportunity to deal with them.

Here's what you do. Set up a folder on the drive where you want to backup your phone's pictures. Using the app, select all the pictures on the phone and copy them to this folder. Let's say you have 500 pictures. The copy will take a while, but you will eventually have all 500 pictures in that folder on the drive. Then a few days later, you want to backup your newer pictures, but you aren't sure exactly which ones are new. Do the same thing you did originally. Using the app, select all the pictures on the phone, and tell the app to copy them to that same folder. After thinking about it for a while, it will tell you that you have selected 541 pictures to copy, but 500 of them have duplicate file names. It will ask you what you want to do about that. Select the "skip" option, and any file with a duplicate file name won't get copied. In this example, it will only copy the 41 pictures that weren't there before.

This works, but it's still not great. It takes a while to analyze the files before starting the copy. Let's say you had 1000 pictures originally, and you only took 2 new ones. The backup should be fast, right? Well, no. It takes the app a surprisingly long time to analyze the 1002 pictures and figure out that 1000 of them have duplicate file names. Eventually, it will tell you about the 1000 duplicates and you can select "skip". Then it will copy only the 2 new pictures. But even though there were only two new pictures, the process takes a frustratingly long time.

If you know exactly which pictures are new, and there aren't very many, you can always just pick those by hand instead of doing the select-all. In that case, the process is very fast since the app is only dealing with the few pictures you selected and not analyzing a 1000 of them.
text_fidelity_b: SanDisk iXpand 16GB Mobile Flash Drive with Lightning Connector for iPhones, iPads & Computers (SDIX-016G-G57)

Kindle Fire HD 8.9", Dolby Audio, Dual-Band Wi-Fi, 32 GB (Previous Generation - 2nd) SEE BELOW FOR LATEST ON 5-3-13
SEE BELOW FOR LATEST ON 5-11-13 SECOND DEVICE GOING BACK TOO. SOUND FAILED.
SEE BELOW FOR FINAL REVIEW, ALL POSITIVE, 5-20-13

5-11-13 I REALLY DON'T KNOW HOW TO RATE THIS THING NOW. WHEN IT RUNS IT IS FINE. WHEN IT DOESN'T IT ISN'T. NOW THE SOUND HAS FAILED. CAN'T RUN PANDORA, ANY WEBSITE THAT PLAYS AN AUDIO TRACK WITH VIDEO OR MUSIC; CAN'T RUN MP3 OR MP4 FILES AND HEAR ANY SOUND. ANOTHER BEING SHIPPED TO ARRIVE HERE TUESDAY. I AM GETTING REALLY TIRED OF REBUILDING MY BOOKMARKS, APPS, PREFERENCES, ETC. I HAVE WASTED HOURS AND HOURS DOING THIS NOW. I WAS EVEN SO HAPPY THIS TIME THAT I BOUGHT MY WIFE A 7" FIRE HD FOR MOTHER'S DAY. I PRAY HER'S WORKS. I HAVE ALMOST COMPLETELY LOST MY FAITH IN FIRE HD.

The above, and the stuff I deleted from my first review had to do with screen flaws in the first and dead sound card in second. All cleared up and the cogent review comes next.

5-20-13

PROBLEMS RESOLVED WITH THIRD DEVICE. WHEN THEY WORK AND WITH SOME APPS TO SPEED THINGS UP, IT IS 5 STARS NOW.

While waiting for the 3rd device I checked around the web for quality issues with other vendors and discovered they all have problems now. The race to grab some market share is pushing new/re-designed devices out too fast and DOA and other issues are rampant in the industry. Amazom actually may be a bit better; the offset is that if you have a problem and get on the phone with them it is pretty easy to get a new device sent out for exchange via 2-day air, and you keep the one you have until the new arrives. That is an industry high mark that not all vendors have. So this took a lot of the sting out of flaws. Enough.

The device is beautiful, powerful and in 32 GB size has enough memory for most of us, even the video users or gamers who save lots of bytes.

I made the best change though by installing the Dolphin browser app and ES File Explorer. Doplpin is faster than Silk and more flexible. Also you can organzie folders for bookmarks very easily. ES File Exp is a tool you need. You can find almost everything on your device easily and manage apps and other files. They are both free and in Amazon store.

I use Last Pass and Xmarks to manage passwords and bookmarks on desktop/laptop machines and they both work very well with Dolphin. So I was able to load a lot of bookmarks easily that otherwise would have been typed in laboriously and taken hours.

I use Gmail because that gives me the perfect multi-platform email program.

I am a Latin student and found a couple of very good Latin apps. I also was able to find The Daily Missal Readings and an app with the Liturgy of the Hours, in both Latin and English. Both available in Amazon Store too.

When in range of Wifi I can do anything I need to do and do it well with the Kindle Fire HD 8.9" When operating stand-alone I have Latin-English books/Bibles on the device and the necessary dictionaries to continue translation. Very handy.

The only fault still, and I have complained about this repeatedly to Amazon, you can look up a foreign word from a book in German, Spanish, Portugese, French and Italian dictionaries, plus several Oriental tongues, but Latin is not a choice. You have to go to the web or type the word out into Google Translate, Whitaker's Words or some online program. It seems it would be easy to add the Latin dictionary as an option because several very good digital versions are around and I use two of them on an e-ink 1st generation Kindle device. Fix that Kindle and you get 10 stars!

In short, buy one but if you have trouble, get to them right away. Of course, read the instructions and make sure your complaint is not from lack of knowledge.

My final words on the subject.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Fire HD 8.9", Dolby Audio, Dual-Band Wi-Fi, 32 GB (Previous Generation - 2nd)

text_fidelity_a:
iHome 2-In-1 Pen Stylus for iPad/iPad 2 and all Touch Screen Devices (IH-IP2202) I expect that no one is going to use a stylus 100% of the time with their touch screen. There are, however, some times when a stylus is more convenient than using your finger. Drawing objects freehand is a common example. Another example is when you need to precisely move objects around the screen (eg in a CAD program) and this is difficult with your finger because your finger blocks your view of the target area.

There are many many touch screen stylus for sale on Amazon. Some cost less than 50 cents each. All the latest stylus have similar round soft touch rubber tips. All seem to work about the same. This iHome stylus doesn't seem to work any better than the others that I have tried.

The iHome stylus is better looking than most of the competition because of the long slim shape with silver-tone accents. Some of the cheap ones look very plasticy (though they do work just as well). Some other stylus are fatter, which makes them easier to grip if you have large hands.

The built-in ball-point pen is a feature that most other stylus do not have. The pen works well, though I do not know how easy ink refills will be to find. There is no literature in the package about what refills it can use.

Is this product worth $15? I have to say no, but I'm a cheapskate. You can decide on value for yourself, but look at the competition first.
text_fidelity_b: iHome 2-In-1 Pen Stylus for iPad/iPad 2 and all Touch Screen Devices (IH-IP2202)

text_fidelity_a:
StarTech.com 2.5in USB 3.0 SSD SATA Hard Drive Enclosure - Storage enclosure with power indicator - 2.5" - SATA 3Gb/s - 3 Gbit/s - USB 3.0 - black (SAT2510BU32) I'm using this enclosure for an earlier-gen SATA thin profile 500GB Western Digital hard drive and getting great results. The fastest removable media I own is a SanDisk Extreme USB 3.0 flash drive. And with this enclosure, the WD hard drive is hitting read/write speeds that are almost as fast as the SanDisk Extreme. It's not nearly SATA III fast (since it's not a SATA III drive), but fast.

I followed the recommendation of other reviewers and reformatted the hard drive to MBR and NTFS file system before using. This requires using DiskPart or Disk Management in Windows. Instructions are available on the web.

Older hard drives with a thick profile won't fit this enclosure. If you're not sure if your hard drive is thin profile and you don't have a metric ruler handy, if it's a quarter inch or less in thickness (and has a SATA connector) it's thin profile and will fit this enclosure.

I did not get good results testing the enclosure with a desktop computer with only USB 2.0 capability---it was very slow or not even recognized when plugged in. I don't want to blame the enclosure, because I've had similar issues with other brand enclosures and that same desktop computer. But I want to mention this in case you're thinking of buying this to use with a computer that only has USB 2.0. You might do better to get a USB 2.0 enclosure.
text_fidelity_b: StarTech.com 2.5in USB 3.0 SSD SATA Hard Drive Enclosure - Storage enclosure with power indicator - 2.5" - SATA 3Gb/s - 3 Gbit/s - USB 3.0 - black (SAT2510BU32)

But in these days of COVID and work-from-home, I was stuck with just my little laptop screen. While my office offered to let me take my monitors home I just didn't have the space, and I do like to occasionally do work at the local cafe or lounge.

Enter this portable screen...

-It plugs into the laptop with just one cable and no separate power cable is needed! All I need to use it is the included USB-C cable and the screen itself!
-It's thin and its lightweight. In fact, it slides into my backpack's laptop pouch and still has room for both my laptop and my buttpad (for hard seating).

My only criticism would be that anytime it gets unplugged from the laptop, the settings reset, and when you plug it back in you have to readjust the settings. It's only 4 button presses to change it which I have down now so its not a big deal but it would be nice if this setting was memorized somehow.

In the days of COVID and WFH, this has been one of the best productivity purchases I've made and it has been beyond worthwhile.

I bought one pair for my front L & R and I was so impressed that I bought another to use as my center channel (they only come in pairs so I have an extra speaker in case I blow one out!). I replaced my Martin Logan center with this (laid on its side) and it handles dialog better. Now all 3 speakers in my front soundstage are these Sonys and my system has never sounded better.

I am not a fan of the grills, the Sony logo looks a bit cheap, so I use them without the grills and they look great.

I don't think these would be great for music, that "warmth" that people love for playing music usually distorts dialog. I only occasionally listen to music on my system and I think they are fine but I wanted to mention that because it might be an issue for some people. These are clear as a bell, keep that in mind.
text_fidelity_b: Sony SSCSE Dolby Atmos Enabled Speakers, Black, Dolby Atmos Enabled Speakers (Pair), 4 Inch (Pack of 2)

Bloody M90 TWS Active Noise Cancelling Bluetooth Gaming Earbuds, Hybrid Carbon Diaphragm, Bass Music & Low Latency Gaming Mode, Dual ENC Microphone, IPX4 Rate, with Wireless Charging Case I’ve been using the Bloody M90 Earbuds for about a month, and I’m quite impressed with them! I usually prefer over-ear headphones because they are more comfortable for me -- I have quite a few inner ear piercings -- but I’ve barely used any other set of headphones for the past month.

Once you find the right size, these buds are comfortable and stay in your ears. The box includes three sizes of ear tips: small, medium, and large. I did have a short adjustment period, the noise cancelling made me nauseated. This is not a fault of the earbuds, it’s something that can happen, and within a week, I was able to wear the earbuds for hours at a time.

I use the earbuds to listen to music and stream shows. I’m not an audiophile, but I think the sound quality is pretty good. Music sounds clear and punchy, no tin can or thin bass here. The noise cancelling is not as robust as a pair of over-ear headphones, but it dampens enough of the background noise in my home that I can clearly hear what I have playing.

The main advantage of these earbuds is they don’t give me a headache like over-ear ones do after a few hours. There’s no headband sitting on top of my head, or squeezy tight ear cups. As I mentioned, I have a few inner ear piercings (tragus, rook, daith) and I’m still able to wear the earbuds comfortably. They stay in while I walk around the house.

I can use one earbud or both, and they have tap controls. They connect easily, all it takes is opening the case and they’re connected to my computer.

The case is pretty swanky, matte black with a thin strip of metallic red. The case has 4 small LEDs on the front to show battery and charging status, the lights go on when opening the case or when it’s charging. The case works with wireless charging or via USB-C, a short cable is included.

The instructions are easy to understand. The Quick Start guide was all I needed to get up and running.

text_fidelity_a:
NETGEAR Orbi Compact Wall-Plug Whole Home Mesh WiFi System - WiFi router and wall-plug satellite extender with speeds up to 2.2 Gbps over 3,500 sq. feet, AC2200 (RBK20W) This is an updated version of a mesh system router and satellite I already have. The technology is great when it's working, but, for whatever reason, my system has needed to be reset once a week or more, and the coverage is nowhere near as good as it claims it should be.

My hope was that the newer version would be faster and have better coverage. It isn't. It doesn't. And, like the earlier version, it has to be in AP mode to work with my FIOS modem (FIOS has a version of this available with its own firmware, but you have to buy a new one, and it won't work with any other ISP). Those hopes dashed, my next hope was that I could at least use the router as a satellite on my existing system, which, of course not.

So, you would think I could at LEAST use the satellite from the new one with the old system or the old satellite with the new one? They are the same model, after all. And that, too, would be a nope.

What I finally did, after hours on the internet (and other hours just trying to set up the new one by itself - it was the same with the old one - it for some reason despises custom settings and will not save them the first many times. It will also lose them after firmware upgrades, I expect, like its predecessor), was set it up alongside the old one with its own network name. Now I have one network serving one side of the house and the other serving the other. Speeds are good. So far, no routing issues, and I don't really expect any. The two network solution seems to have worked well for others.

But really.

If you are looking to expand your Orbi network, check out the nighthawk mesh expanders. I have the 7500, and it's excellent. Also, don't take my lukewarm review for a no-rec. The Orbi is, as far as I can tell from personal experience, buggy and locked down, but, again from personal experience, it beats the Velop (its nearest competitor) by a mile for coverage.
text_fidelity_b: NETGEAR Orbi Compact Wall-Plug Whole Home Mesh WiFi System - WiFi router and wall-plug satellite extender with speeds up to 2.2 Gbps over 3,500 sq. feet, AC2200 (RBK20W)

text_fidelity_a:
TCL 65" Class 4-Series 4K UHD HDR Roku 2017 Smart TV - 65S405 Was hesitant to buy a not so known brand. However for the most part its a really good TV. Did some research on TCL and found out that several tv brands were in fact manufactered by TCL. Emerson, RCA, Phillips etc.

I did pay extra for a entended warranty because the last 2 tv's I owned both went to the recycle bin in about 2.5 years. However, the extended warranty for parts and labor worked out to be about 10$ a year. The Insurance company figures that the failure rate isnt going to be that significant based on how low the cost for the warranty.

The remote and the menus on the TV dont have much functionality. I guess Roku thought that having a more plug and play approach would be better. The app for your mobile device has that functionality though. Can change picture settings etc. I have yet to find the sound options though. Be aware that going to external speakers via audio out also cuts off the internal speakers. Picture quality is really good overall. There are times though that it appears to be trying to upconvert to the 4K from a lower definition video stream and when it does there are some interesting visual artifacts. I don't know why but I think that some streaming services have encoded the audio of their content differently due to needing to increase volume on TV from say 35 to 95 in order to hear it. As a example Netflix volume on tv 35 to 40.. Amazon prime I have to increase volume to 90 or higher to achieve same level of hearing as Netflix. There are variations of course but generally speaking over the entirety of the video libraries of both services thats what I have to do. Blue ray is fantastic through TV.

I do have several years experience with roku streaming devices and those do work well and I have never had a hardware failure in them. I would suggest setting up a roku account before initializing TV. Makes setup way easier.

Havent been able to notice a difference between wired connection and wired as far as visually or sonically.

Overall, for a 55 inch class TV for the price.. Decent deal. Will have to see how the hardware lasts.
text_fidelity_b: TCL 65" Class 4-Series 4K UHD HDR Roku 2017 Smart TV - 65S405
